translationRepairs: Xiangzi heaved a deep sigh, and tears fell from his eyes. "Alas, Yu Rang!" he cried.
Xiangzi heaved a deep sigh, and tears fell from his eyes. "Alas, Yu-zi!" he cried.
Xiangzi’s vocative is 豫子, the honorific, not the personal name 豫讓. Rendering it as “Yu Rang” misstates what he cried.

Nie Zheng replied, "Han and Wei are not far apart. Now, to assassinate a state's prime minister — a man who is kin to the ruler — this cannot be done with a crowd. With too many people, something will go wrong. If something goes wrong, word will leak out. And if word leaks, all of Han will rise against you as an enemy. Would that not be catastrophic?"

Nie Zheng replied, "Han and Wey are not far apart. Now, to assassinate a state's prime minister — a man who is kin to the ruler — this cannot be done with a crowd. With too many people, something will go wrong. If something goes wrong, word will leak out. And if word leaks, all of Han will rise against you as an enemy. Would that not be catastrophic?"
The source is 韓之與衛, the state 衛 (Wey), not 魏. In this chapter 伐魏 later uses the same English “Wei” for a different polity, so the original collapse is a naming error.
His forebears were originally from Qi but had migrated to Wei. The people of Wei knew him by the name Qingqing.
His forebears were originally from Qi but had migrated to Wei. The people of Wei knew him by the name Qing Qing.
衛人謂之慶卿 names him Qing plus the honorific 卿, parallel to 荊卿 in the next sentence. Fusing the two syllables as Qingqing invents a personal name the Chinese does not give.
Afterward, Qin conquered Wei and established the Eastern Commandery, relocating the collateral kinsmen of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
Afterward, Qin attacked Wei and established the Eastern Commandery, relocating the collateral kinsmen of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
秦伐魏 is a campaign against Wei, not the extinction of the state. The same sentence still treats 衞元君’s collateral line as relocatable, which “conquered” overstates.
Later, Qin conquered Wei, established the Eastern Commandery, and relocated the branch relatives of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
Later, Qin attacked Wei, established the Eastern Commandery, and relocated the branch relatives of Duke Yuan of Wei to Ye Wang.
The literal field has the same over-reading: 伐 means attacked, not conquered.

Once Jing Ke was seated, the Crown Prince left his own seat, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "Master Tian, despite my unworthiness, enabled you to come before me so that I might dare to voice this plan. Surely this is Heaven's way of showing pity on Yan and not forsaking its orphaned people.

Once Jing Ke was seated, the Crown Prince left his own seat, bowed his head to the floor, and said, "Master Tian, not knowing my unworthiness, enabled you to come before me so that I might dare to voice this plan. Surely this is Heaven's way of showing pity on Yan and not forsaking its orphan.

The original drops 不知, turning Tian Guang’s ignorance of Dan’s unworthiness into a concessive “despite,” and it invents “orphaned people” for 其孤. The repair restores both the negation and the singular orphaned remnant.
Jing Ke pursued the King of Qin, and the king fled around a bronze pillar.
Jing Ke pursued the King of Qin, and the king fled around a pillar.
秦王環柱而走 names only a pillar. “Bronze” is not in this sentence and is an invented material detail.
Crippled, Jing Ke hurled the dagger at the King of Qin. It missed, striking a bronze pillar instead.
Crippled, Jing Ke hurled the dagger at the King of Qin. It missed, striking a paulownia pillar instead.
The supplied text is 中桐柱, a paulownia pillar (桐), not a bronze pillar (銅). The original English misreads the graph.
Jing Ke, crippled, hurled his dagger at the King of Qin but missed, striking a bronze pillar instead.
Jing Ke, crippled, hurled his dagger at the King of Qin but missed, striking a paulownia pillar instead.
The literal field repeats the same misreading of 桐柱 as bronze rather than paulownia.
